title: Virata: the year in disguise
hook: Kichaka kicks Sairandhri in front of the king, and the man at the dice table tells her to go inside
carry: once again she's the one who speaks

segments.voice: Yesterday: the weapons went up into the shami tree, and the Pandavas walked into Virata's city one at a time. Your line was keep only themselves.
screen: `VIRATA: THE YEAR IN DISGUISE.` · `THE WEAPONS IN THE SHAMI TREE.`

segments.voice: The disguises have held for months. Then the queen's brother comes to visit. His name is Kichaka. He commands King Virata's army, and the court is a little afraid of him. He sees the maid Sairandhri and wants her. She refuses him, plainly, and tells him she's protected. He doesn't care. He goes to his sister, the queen, and the queen sends Sairandhri to his house on an errand, to fetch wine. Draupadi knows exactly what this errand is.
screen: `THE QUEEN'S BROTHER, KICHAKA.` → `SHE REFUSES HIM.` → `AN ERRAND THAT IS A TRAP.`

segments.voice: At Kichaka's house he grabs at her. She breaks free and runs, straight into the royal court, where King Virata sits with Kanka beside him at the dice. Kichaka chases her in, catches her by the hair, and kicks her to the floor in front of everyone. And here the epic does something painful. It shows us the brothers. Bhima is there, and his face darkens, and he stares at a big tree as if he means to tear it up and use it as a club. Yudhishthira sees it. Quietly, as Kanka, he presses Bhima's toe and says something like: looking for firewood, cook? Go cut your trees somewhere else. But Draupadi doesn't stay quiet. From the floor she speaks to the king, in his own court. What kind of king lets a woman be struck in front of him and does nothing? Is this how justice works in the Matsya court? A queen once dragged into one assembly hall is struck in another, and once again she's the one who speaks. Then Kanka turns to her. Go to the queen's rooms, he tells her. Your Gandharva husbands will act when the time is right. You're interrupting the king's game. It sounds cold. It's meant to. One word of recognition and the whole year is lost. The disguise holds. But the epic makes sure we feel what it costs, and who pays.
screen: `A CHASE INTO THE COURT` · `BHIMA STARES AT A TREE` · `DRAUPADI SPEAKS TO THE KING` · then, large: `KANKA: GO INSIDE, NOT NOW`

segments.voice: Let your hands rest open on your knees, and bring to mind a moment when you had to hold back, or when you wished someone had spoken for you; don't relive it, just let it be named. Breathing in, feel how much holding back weighs, and breathing out, let your hands stay open. If you pray, you can bring the people who carry that kind of weight into your prayer.
Virata. The king whose court sees a maid struck and stays still, and the place where Draupadi asks what kind of justice that is.
Your line: once again she's the one who speaks. Struck to the floor, she still asked for justice. Until tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 809 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: VIRATA: THE YEAR IN DISGUISE.`

howItsDone: The Kichaka episode is retold and staged in Indian performance traditions, and readers of the epic discuss Yudhishthira's restraint and Draupadi's protest side by side.

fork.setup: you're Yudhishthira, disguised as Kanka. your wife is struck in front of you. if you're recognized, the exile starts over. what do you do?
options: stand up and reveal who you are.
send her to the queen's rooms and say the time will come.
leave the court without a word.
fork.reveal: he keeps the disguise, tells her the Gandharvas will act in time, and even stops Bhima. the text lets it look as cold as it is.

trapdoor: what you thought: Yudhishthira didn't care what happened to Draupadi.
what it means: one word of recognition would undo the whole year; his restraint has a price, and she pays it.
what a scholar hears: a second hall, a second insult: Draupadi questioning a king in court recalls her questions in the dice hall.
guess: the Matsya king, whose court sees Sairandhri struck
the general who commands the Matsya army
the hall where the Pandavas first lost at dice

chat.says: When Kichaka hurt Draupadi in court, why did Yudhishthira send her away instead of helping?
options: One word of recognition would end their year in hiding; the story shows what that cost her.
He didn't believe her account and thought she had started the trouble herself.
He was afraid of Kichaka and didn't want to anger the army's commander.
chat.meaning: As Kanka, Yudhishthira couldn't be recognized, or the year in hiding would be lost. The disguise held, and the epic makes us feel what it cost Draupadi.

Kichaka.meaning: the queen's brother, commander of King Virata's army

Sairandhri.meaning: Draupadi's disguise: a maid who dresses the queen's hair

Kanka.meaning: Yudhishthira's disguise: a Brahmin who plays dice with the king

Matsya.meaning: the kingdom ruled by King Virata

Gandharva.meaning: a heavenly being; Draupadi says her husbands are Gandharvas

recall: fire-sticks for kindling a sacred fire
bites Nala and changes his shape
